::: {.statx-chapter-banner}
## Make uncertainty observable

This lab will connect probability calculations to repeated experiments, helping students see long-run behavior emerge from randomness.
:::

## Learning objectives

By the end of this lab, students will be able to:

1. Construct a sample space and calculate event probabilities.
2. Distinguish conditional, joint, and marginal probabilities.
3. Use Bayes' theorem to update a probability after observing evidence.
4. Simulate Bernoulli, binomial, Poisson, uniform, and normal outcomes.

## Planned workflow

::: {.statx-topic-grid}
::: {.statx-topic-card}
### 1. Coin and dice experiments

Compare theoretical probabilities with empirical proportions from repeated trials.
:::

::: {.statx-topic-card}
### 2. Conditional probability

Build a two-way table and interpret probabilities with changing reference groups.
:::

::: {.statx-topic-card}
### 3. Bayes in context

Update an initial belief using the sensitivity and specificity of a screening procedure.
:::

::: {.statx-topic-card}
### 4. Distribution gallery

Simulate common discrete and continuous distributions and compare their shapes.
:::
:::

## Deliverables

- A simulation-versus-theory comparison
- A conditional-probability table
- One Bayesian update explained in plain language
- A panel of distribution plots
